MongoDB discontinued on-premises Charts in September 2021. A MongoDB staff member wrote on 2022-02-01: "The on-prem version was discontinued last September. We did include a notice about this for around a year before support ended." Since on-prem Charts ended, cloud Charts reads Atlas deployments: clusters and federated database instances, including Online Archives. A locally hosted MongoDB server cannot be a data source. On 2021-05-10 a MongoDB staff member replied: "You'll need to copy the data from your personal cluster into the Atlas cluster first." MongoDB has deprecated iframe embedding

Unauthenticated embedding is documented as less secure and should be used only for charts that display non-sensitive data. By default, embedded charts allow no filter fields until the author allows at least one. "Allow all fields in the data source used in this chart" is an alternative that allows every field. Allowing an embedded-document field does not allow its sub-fields; each must be listed separately, so adding only `favorites` does not permit filtering on `favorites.color`. For authenticated embedding, MongoDB documents an injected function that can read the caller's token via `context.

Charts builds one aggregation pipeline per chart. The segment order is: charts views, embedding pre-filters, dashboard filters, chart query, lookup fields, calculated fields, embedding filters (including injected filters), chart filters, encoded fields, sorting, then the maximum document limit. Charts skips any segment the author did not configure. Authors can inspect the generated pipeline with "View Aggregation Pipeline" in the Chart Builder. **Scope.** In: the mechanisms that make a Charts usage pattern harmful, their limits, history, failure modes and disagreements. Out: siblings (SDK/REST surface, access control, cost model, chart-type catalogue, auth providers), general MongoDB schema anti-patterns and general query tuning. The parent's heatmap row and `tenantId: 'acme'` snippet are not counted as evidence. Claims that refine them are listed under Deltas.

In scope: the operational anti-patterns in Atlas Charts, meaning query shape, pipeline ordering, indexing, result-size limits, caching and refresh, workload placement, embedding authentication, and filter security. For each one the report covers the trade-off, how to check for it, and what it means in practice.

Out of scope: sibling concepts (the cost model, analytics-node configuration, the Embedding SDK API as a whole, chart types), general MongoDB schema anti-patterns (Atlas Performance Advisor), and general aggregation tuning.
